thread:
incident-bot: [PAGER] p99 streaming latency SLO breach on shared-gpu-pool-2. p95 160ms -> 950ms, p99 320ms -> 5.3s. Streaming stalls and delayed first-chunk observed. Affected endpoints: /v1/stream, /v1/chat. Pager: @leah. Dash: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/pool2

leah: ack. Joining. Any 500s thrown?

tom: no 500s, just long gaps. p50 fine. Looks like tail I/O or GPU link saturation. Packet drops low.

priya: I'm seeing heavy NVMe write throughput on host-7 and host-8 during the breach windows. `iostat -x 1` shows util ~99% and avgqu-sz spiking.

ops-sre: kernel logs on host-8: repeated `blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1` and `blkio: task blocked for more than 120 seconds`. Could be device-level degradation or extreme write contention from one pod.

leah: list top GPU processes: `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_gpu_memory,process_name --format=csv` -> tenant-halo has multiple long-running processes across gpus on host-7/8. Also see large checkpoint writes to `/data/checkpoints/halo/`.

priya: tenant-halo currently ~48% of token volume on pool-2 and frequently checkpoints every 7m. That lines up with stalls.

tom: mitigation proposal: 1) soft-throttle tenant-halo IO via cgroup v2 io.weight, 2) temporarily migrate tenant-halo pods to dedicated-io nodes, 3) apply streaming fallback to smaller quantized model for non-critical routes, 4) suppress noisy alerts while we stabilize.

leah: doing io.weight change on host-7: `systemd-run --scope --property=IOWeight=1000 sleep 1` won't work for containers. We'll patch the pod's systemd slice via kubernetes CR. Applying patch now via `kubectl patch deployment halo --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"io.weight":"200"}}}}}'`.

ops-sre: note: some nodes still use cgroup v1. Use `echo 200 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/halo.slice/blkio.weight` as fallback. I'll detect host family and apply both where needed.

priya: scaling halo replicas down to 1 on shared pool and scheduling rest to `nodeSelector: dedicated-io=true`. Triggered reschedule on host-8.

tom: routing change: set `/v1/stream` fallback to `rw-small-cpu` when GPU queue depth > 30. Applied via routing service. This should remove heavy GPU kernels for some requests.

incident-bot: Alert suppression: pool-2 suppressed for 20m.

support: opening customer incidents: CS-4910 (halo), CS-4911 (sparrow). Informing accounts: "We're mitigating streaming degradation due to infrastructure contention; working on migration and hardware checks."

priya: after throttling and migration p99 decreased from 5.3s -> 1.8s in 2 minutes. p95 ~420ms. Streaming chunk spacing improved to <700ms.

ops-sre: discovered NVMe SMART warnings on host-8 nvme0n1: increased media errors. Filing vendor ticket NVME-7933 and scheduling replacement. Also found `dmesg` showing recurring timeouts on the drive.

leah: I'm going to set a targeted traffic split: 25% diverted to pool-4 to reduce load on pool-2 while we observe. Applying via traffic router: `traffic.rules.pool2.split=75/25`.

tom: also throttle checkpointing frequency in tenant-halo job by toggling runtime flag `HALO_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL=900` to spread writes. Pushed flag to their job template.

priya: monitoring shows IO await normalizing on host-7/8. p99 now oscillating 1.2s -> 1.9s. Keep watching GPU link util; still somewhat elevated but not saturating.

ops-sre: vendor ticket NVME-7933 created. Recommend we avoid scheduling new pods with heavy PVs on host-8 until replacement. Marked node as `avoid-pv-scheduling=true` in node labels.

leah: customer impact summary for ops/comms: tenant-halo (evicted/throttled), tenant-sparrow (minor), tenant-ivy (minor). Support tickets CS-4910, CS-4911. No lost data, transient stalls only. Draft to customers: "We've mitigated the majority of the latency and are migrating heavy workloads to dedicated hardware. We'll follow up with remediation timeline."

tom: performance note: add a guardrail to autoscaler: don't pack >2 IO-intense pods on same NVMe host. Might prevent recurrence.

priya: post-incident action items: 1) add per-tenant sustained write rate alert (>=150MB/s for 2m), 2) extend runbook with cgroup v2 commands and examples for k8s patches, 3) add route fallback hysteresis to avoid oscillation, 4) audit autoscaler binpack policy. I'll own the alerts and runbook updates.

ops-sre: I'll coordinate NVMe replacement and vendor RMAs. Also add a script to detect concurrent heavy checkpoint writes and auto-evict one tenant if thresholds exceeded.

incident-bot: Severity downgraded to Sev3 (mitigated -> monitoring). Page will auto-close in 40m if stable.

oncall-bot: Handoff: @leah -> @tom at 16:20 UTC.

leah: final: keep an eye on p99 above 2s and any sudden NVMe re-errors. Great work everyone. :thumbsup:

end of thread
